title: Density-driven reversal of flavour-entanglement anisotropy in the D3-D7 holographic conductor
abstract: We study the leading probe-flavour contribution to equal-time spatial entanglement entropy in a homogeneous 3+1-dimensional strongly coupled conductor at finite temperature and charge density, realised holographically by the D3-D7 system and driven by a constant DC electric field. We compare slab-shaped subregions that are extended in two spatial directions and have finite width parallel or transverse to the field. The difference between the corresponding entropy corrections isolates a homogeneous, spatially traceless response and exhibits a density-driven sign reversal. Over the investigated parameter range, the crossover density increases with the electric-field magnitude and decreases with the strip width. Mutual information shows the same qualitative reversal and provides an ultraviolet-finite check. We trace the effect to a radial sign competition in the full Dirac-Born-Infeld stress anisotropy. The reversal is a smooth response crossover rather than a thermodynamic phase transition.
summary: This theoretical work uses the AdS/CFT correspondence via the D3-D7 system to study entanglement entropy in a current-carrying, strongly coupled conductor. The authors find that the entanglement anisotropy undergoes a smooth sign reversal as the charge density changes. This reversal is fundamentally linked to the stress tensor anisotropy of the holographic source, providing insights into non-equilibrium quantum correlations.
main_problem: The study investigates how a conserved charge density modifies the orientation dependence of equal-time spatial entanglement entropy in a non-equilibrium steady state (NESS) within a strongly coupled conductor.
main_result: The anisotropy in the entanglement entropy exhibits a density-driven sign reversal, which is traced to a radial sign competition in the full Dirac-Born-Infeld stress anisotropy. This reversal is a smooth crossover, not a phase transition.
method: Holographic entanglement entropy is calculated using the Ryu–Takayanagi/HRT prescription, focusing on the leading probe-flavour correction derived from the linearized closed-string response.
model_or_system: The system is modeled by the D3–D7 holographic conductor, representing a strongly coupled $3+1$ dimensional conductor at finite temperature and charge density, driven by a DC electric field.
key_observables: Leading probe-flavour contribution to equal-time spatial entanglement entropy, mutual information anisotropy, and the difference in entropy corrections for parallel vs. transverse subregions ($\Delta S_{\parallel} - \Delta S_{\perp}$).
important_parameters: Electric field magnitude ($E$), charge density ($\mu$), and the width ($\ell$) of the subregions being compared.
main_assumptions: The calculation is performed at leading order in the probe expansion, and the analysis isolates the homogeneous, spatially traceless response by taking the difference between two orientations.
figures_summary: Figure 1 schematically illustrates the geometry used for calculating the entropy difference for parallel and transverse orientations relative to the electric field.
paper_structure: The paper develops the holographic framework for calculating entanglement entropy in a driven, non-equilibrium state, focusing on isolating the anisotropy via the difference between parallel and transverse cuts, leading to the identification of the density-dependent crossover mechanism.
why_interesting: The concept of entanglement anisotropy in non-equilibrium systems is highly relevant to understanding quantum correlations in driven quantum materials, providing a holographic tool to diagnose directional dependence.
